name: Second Visit
who: Local businesses with repeat-purchase potential and a customer list nobody is using — salons, garages, dental and physio practices, restaurants, pet care.
problem: "We've got two thousand names in the system. We paid to get every one of them, and we have never sent them anything. Some of them haven't been in for two years and I couldn't tell you why."
solution: Done-for-you lifecycle messaging: a win-back campaign to everyone who has lapsed, a follow-up after every visit, and a small calendar of seasonal and birthday offers. We write it, run it, and report the revenue it brought back in euros.
promise: You paid to win every name in that customer list, and have never sent them anything. We bring back the customers you already paid for, and report what came back in euros.
gets:
A win-back campaign to your lapsed customers, written and sent for you
An after-visit follow-up and a seasonal calendar that runs itself
A monthly report in euros: customers returned and revenue recovered
positioning: Reported in recovered revenue rather than opens and clicks, which is what makes the retainer survive a bad month.
voice: Warm and concrete. Talks about customers by name and about euros by number.
channels: Existing client base, POS and booking-software user groups, local business associations
